method: All 1,108 visible records checked against explicit publication-title and curated sample descriptions and matching Europe PMC/MEDLINE age indexing. Available abstract and curated-summary age ranges were inspected in context. Source-indexed ages describe coverage, not an exclusively age-specific sample or effect.

definitions.children: Publication wording or NLM infant/child indexing; explicit sample ages up to 12 also qualify.
definitions.adolescents: Publication wording or NLM Adolescent indexing (13–18); explicit sample ranges overlapping 13–18 also qualify.
definitions.youth: Discovery umbrella for explicit youth/young-people wording, adolescent indexing and young-adult indexing (19–24), plus explicit sample ranges overlapping those ages. Source definitions vary; a youth focus is distinguished from inclusion in a broader sample.
definitions.adults: Publication wording or NLM Adult, Young Adult, Middle Aged or Aged indexing, plus explicit sample ages 19 or above. Older adults also appear here.
definitions.older-adults: Publication wording or NLM Aged indexing (65+), plus explicit sample ages 65 or above. Some sources explicitly describe younger thresholds as older adults; their reported ranges remain visible.
definitions.not-specified: No supported human age group identified from the checked text/indexing, or source identity/nonhuman evidence prevents a human-age assignment. This does not mean that the full publication never states ages.

pmid-32892758.reason: The abstract explicitly recruits adults. The Child indexing term concerns the historical trauma, not a child study population.

pmid-20117669.reason: The intervention targets children and adolescents; parents provide reports. Adult indexing does not establish an adult intervention cohort.
